First release of this go2rtc fork with a **native Reolink Baichuan source** (`bc://`).

Reolink cameras can now be used straight from go2rtc over the protocol the Reolink apps use, without the cameras' RTSP or FLV
endpoints and without a neolink → go2rtc chain. Frigate and Home Assistant consume the streams like any other go2rtc stream.

Based on upstream go2rtc 1.9.14 (`master` at c245815).

## Credits

**Protocol reference: my own documentation in
[privatecoder/neolink `docs/`](https://github.com/privatecoder/neolink/tree/master/docs).** I wrote it in my neolink fork
after forking, from disassembly and packet captures of the official Reolink client and from the neolink source. It is the
reference this source was implemented and reviewed against, and where sources disagreed it was the deciding one:
[bc-protocol](https://github.com/privatecoder/neolink/blob/master/docs/bc-protocol.md),
[media-streams](https://github.com/privatecoder/neolink/blob/master/docs/media-streams.md),
[discovery-handshake](https://github.com/privatecoder/neolink/blob/master/docs/discovery-handshake.md),
[connection-modes](https://github.com/privatecoder/neolink/blob/master/docs/connection-modes.md),
[connection-and-bandwidth](https://github.com/privatecoder/neolink/blob/master/docs/connection-and-bandwidth.md),
[two-way-audio](https://github.com/privatecoder/neolink/blob/master/docs/two-way-audio.md),
[av-timestamping](https://github.com/privatecoder/neolink/blob/master/docs/av-timestamping.md) and
[reolink.md](https://github.com/privatecoder/neolink/blob/master/docs/reolink.md).

Findings from my fork that this release relies on:

- **The UDP ACK receive-rate field.** Upstream called it `maybe_latency`. I identified it as the receiver's measured bytes
  per second, which the camera's congestion control uses as its bandwidth estimate. Reporting the real rate is what lets
  4K main streams run at full bitrate over P2P instead of being throttled.
- **Relay/lookup region selection** (`region` here, `relay_server_region` in neolink).
- **The A/V timestamping model**: audio paced by its own content clock and anchored to video, without drift.
- **The mapping of the third stream to the official app's "Balanced" live quality**, and its behaviour.

**Upstream neolink** by George Hilliard (thirtythreeforty), Andrew King (QuantumEntangledAndy) and contributors did the
original reverse engineering of the Baichuan protocol: message framing, login and encryption, the BcMedia format, UDP
discovery with hole punch and relay, and talk with ADPCM. That work predates my fork. Code in `pkg/bc` is ported from it, and
the packet samples used as test data come from it.

## Highlights

- **Local cameras over TCP** (port 9000): login with legacy upgrade, XOR, AES and full-AES encryption.
- **Remote cameras by UID** over Reolink's P2P service: LAN broadcast, hole punch to the public address, or relay. The final
  connection is direct whenever the punch succeeds.
- **Streams**: `main`, `sub` and `extern` ("Balanced"); H.264 and H.265 video; AAC audio, and ADPCM converted to PCMA.
- **Two-way audio**: go2rtc's backchannel is sent to the camera speaker.
- **Stable through reconnects**: video watchdog, timestamps and AAC RTP sequence numbers continue per source, keyframes always
  carry the current parameter sets, and codec or resolution changes are detected.

## Usage

```yaml
streams:
  cam:        bc://user:pass@192.168.1.50                   # main stream, port 9000
  cam_sub:    bc://user:pass@192.168.1.50?stream=sub
  cam_bal:    bc://user:pass@192.168.1.50?stream=extern     # Balanced
  remote:     bc://user:pass@95270000ABCDEFGH                # by UID over P2P
  remote_lan: bc://user:pass@95270000ABCDEFGH?discovery=local&addr=192.168.1.50
```

Options: `stream`, `channel`, `encryption`, `discovery` (`local|remote|map|relay`), `addr`, `region`. The documentation includes a guide to choosing the connection (by IP, LAN broadcast by UID, hole punch, relay), Frigate and Home Assistant setup, and troubleshooting:
[internal/bc/README.md](https://github.com/privatecoder/go2rtc/blob/v1.9.15-baichuan.1/internal/bc/README.md).

To get audio over WebRTC (Home Assistant, Frigate two-way talk), add an Opus track next to the camera's AAC:

```yaml
streams:
  cam:
    - bc://user:pass@192.168.1.50?stream=main
    - ffmpeg:cam#audio=opus
```

**Frigate**: save `go2rtc_linux_amd64` (or `_arm64`) as `/config/go2rtc`, make it executable (`chmod 755`) and restart
Frigate.

## Tested

- Remote cameras by UID: direct P2P in about 1.3 s; 4K H.265 main at about 4.3 Mbit/s and 20 fps; soaks of 30 min (3 streams)
  and 20 min (4 streams) without reconnects or warnings.
- Local camera over TCP: main, sub and Balanced; a 10 min main+sub soak without reconnects.
- Unit and integration tests with the race detector, against a simulated camera over TCP and UDP.

## Known limitations

- Two-way audio has been verified against the simulated camera only, not yet on a real speaker.
- Not supported: PTZ, motion events, SD-card playback and camera settings.

Binaries are built by GitHub Actions from this tag. Linux and FreeBSD are plain executables; Windows and macOS are zipped.
`SHA256SUMS.txt` lists the checksums.
